newsitem.title: USA: Montana winter wheat seeding behind normal pace.
newsitem.headline: Montana winter wheat seeding behind normal pace.

text.p: Seeding of winter wheat in Montana continued to run behind normal with the weather cool and patchy rainfall reported, the Agricultural Statistics Service said.
Winter wheat was 32 percent seeded as of Sunday, up from 12 percent a week earlier but behind last year's 55 percent and the five-year average of 49 percent.
"Winter wheat seeding continues with some growers worried about the late seeding," it said. Wheat had emerged on six percent of the intended acreage, versus a normal 13 percent.
Topsoil moisture was rated eight percent very short, 30 percent short, 61 percent adequate and one percent surplus.
Spring wheat was 99 percent harvested, up from an average of 85 percent, and barley was 97 percent combined, compared with a normal 87 percent.
The sugar beet harvest made some progress with eight percent complete, up from five percent a week earlier. It fell, however, behind last year's 10 percent and the five-year average of nine percent.
